title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous pages). Y is a closed subset of a space X. T is a conic ('cônique', formerly 'tubulaire') neighbourhood of Y in X. Concretely, T is a neighbourhood of Y with a structure of mapping cylinder of a map Ṫ → Y. It carries a multiplication by λ ∈ I = [0,1], with 0·T = Y, T_λ = λT and Ṫ_λ = λṪ (the 'level λ' copy of Ṫ). T̊ = T \ Ṫ is the 'open' part. The previous page noted two things: for λ < 1 the frontier of T_λ is Ṫ_λ, but this fails for λ = 1. It also defined a closed Y ⊂ X to be a 'partie bonne' if it has a collar ('voisinage cylindrique') T ≅ Y × I with Y ↦ Y × {0}.

This page defines X* = X \ T̊ = (X \ T) ∪ Ṫ, which is closed in X. It then states a proposition: for a fixed λ ∈ ]0,1[ the following are equivalent.
(a) Ṫ is collared ('partie bonne') in X*.
(b) Some self-homeomorphism of X carries (T, Ṫ) onto (T_λ, Ṫ_λ).
(b') The same, with the homeomorphism equal to the identity on T_λ' for a given 0 < λ' < λ.
(c) T extends outward: there is a conic neighbourhood T' of Y with T = λT', the identification being compatible with the conic structures.
T is then called a strict conic neighbourhood.

Corollary 1: for strict T, Ṫ is the topological frontier of T in X.
Corollary 2: for any conic T, every T_λ with 0 < λ < 1 is strict (take T' = T with the rescaled structure).
A diagonal marginal note proposes defining strict conic neighbourhoods instead as germs of conic neighbourhoods, i.e. passing to germs as λ varies.

Proofs, in modern terms.
- (b)⇒(a): φ maps X* onto X \ T̊_λ, and in X \ T̊_λ the levels [λ,1] of T give a collar of Ṫ_λ.
- (a)⇒(c): glue the collar Ṫ × [0,1] ⊂ X* to T along Ṫ. This gives a larger mapping cylinder; rescaling its parameter gives T' with T = λT'.
- (c)⇒(b'): use a radial reparametrisation h of [0,1] that is the identity on [0,λ'] and near 1 and sends λ to λ². Apply it in T' and extend by the identity outside.

Purpose: this is the foundational layer of the 'déploiement' (unfolding) of stratified spaces. Strict conic neighbourhoods are the ones that can be cut out cleanly, so that the complement X* is a space with collared boundary Ṫ. This is what is needed for the inductive 'excision of strata' that turns a stratified space into a manifold-with-corners-like object.
errors: (c)⇒(b') needs care. The stretching homeomorphism must be the identity near the outer level of T', and must only move levels where T' is genuinely interior in X. With the convention (previous page) that T̊_μ is open for μ < 1, choosing the support inside levels [λ', μ] with μ < 1 works; this is implicit, not stated.
Corollary 2 tacitly rescales the conic structure: T_λ carries the structure t ↦ (multiplication by t) restricted to T_λ, reparametrised by λ. Harmless but unstated.
Corollary 1 relies on (7) from the previous page (frontier of T_μ is Ṫ_μ for μ < 1) applied to T', together with T = λT'. Correct, but stated without proof.

ideas.what: Complement X* = X \ T̊ of the open part of a conic (mapping-cylinder) neighbourhood, a closed space with 'boundary' Ṫ
ideas.modern_name: Exterior / deleted neighbourhood complement (the 'blow-up' or unfolding step of a stratified space)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 mentions the 'déploiement' of tame stratified spaces in general terms only

ideas.what: Equivalence of collaredness of Ṫ in X*, isotopic shrinkability T → T_λ, and outward extendability T = λT'
ideas.modern_name: Mapping-cylinder neighbourhood with collared boundary / extendable regular neighbourhood
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore of PL/topological regular neighbourhoods (Whitehead, Brown's collaring theorem 1962, Siebenmann)

ideas.what: Strict conic neighbourhoods: Ṫ is the frontier; every T_λ, λ < 1, is strict
Marginal proposal to work with germs of conic neighbourhoods rather than individual ones
ideas.modern_name: Germs of tubular neighbourhoods / control data up to germ equivalence

missed.claim: Grothendieck flags that strict conic neighbourhoods should rather be defined as germs. This is a rethinking of the foundational definition that is not carried out on this page; the following pages continue with the non-germ version.
missed.quote: Il vaut mieux de définir les voisinages côniques stricts comme ... germes de voisinages
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It matches the later germ formalism of Mather/Thom and the ∞-categorical exit-path approach. It offers minor historical evidence of how Grothendieck intended to set up the déploiement, but it is not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful, correct but routine point-set lemma about collared mapping-cylinder neighbourhoods. The content is standard in topological stratification theory (Siebenmann, Quinn); its only interest is as part of Grothendieck's unpublished foundations for the déploiement announced in the Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: (a) most likely reads 'partie-bonne' (the notion just defined on the previous page as collared subset), not 'partie-bord'.
(c) ending likely reads 'l'isomorphisme étant compatible avec les structures de voisinages côniques' rather than 'd'isomorphismes étant compatibles'.
Second corollary: 'Si T voisinage cônique de Y dans X' (the struck word is 'est').

Marginal diagonal note roughly: 'Il vaut mieux définir les voisinages côniques stricts comme germes de voisinages ... pour ... (ε>0)'; the parameter in parentheses is uncertain, possibly '(ε>0)' or '(λ>1)'.
